## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aṭṭhipuñja Sutta* ("A Heap of Bones", Iti 24) is a short discourse located in the first division of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 17). The teaching underscores the immense scope of transmigration (*saṁsāra*) by stating that over the course of wandering in rebirth, a single individual would accumulate a heap of bones as large as a mountain, assuming the bones were preserved and assembled together. The text is also cited in early paracanonical and exegetical works, including the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37).
